pages.text: Greek temples belong to villages. The $(l)village altar$() in front of the acropolis is where villagers pray, and where you make offerings and dedicate relics.$(br2)Receive the $(l)temple priest$()'s blessing and you become a $(l)devotee$() of that village: its prayers bring you $(l)favor$().

A village can have several devotees. Each prayer gives every devotee a full share of favor; the favor is not divided between them.$(br2)You can be devoted to several villages: choose $(l)Become a devotee here$() at another village's priest, or hold a promotion or consecration there. Villagers only go to pray if the village has at least one devotee.

A new village without an acropolis uses its $(l)foundation stone$() as the altar; offerings work there too.$(br2)To leave, press $(l)Stop devotion here$() in the temple inspector. Your relics there are returned to you, and you can come back through the priest later.

In Greek custom the altar stood in the open before the temple door, so the smoke of sacrifice could rise straight to the sky.$(br2)A new village without a temple brings its offerings to Hestia's common hearth. At every sacrifice, the Greeks honored Hestia first.
